museum.text: What is the diagnosis of the arrowed lesion?
options: Dilated, tortuous veins bulging under the esophageal mucosa
Dilated, tortuous lymphatics bulging under the esophageal mucosa
Elongated, tortuous arteries bulging under the gastric mucosa
Elongated, ulcerated veins projecting into the gastric lumen
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Lower end of esophagus opened longitudinally showing multiple prominent, bluish, elongated, tortuous, dilated submucosal veins bulging beneath the mucosal surface, characteristic of esophageal varices.
museum.keyConcept: Esophageal varices: Submucosal venous tortuosity at the lower third of the esophagus due to portal hypertension (porto-systemic shunting).

options: Thickened longitudinal mucosal folds of the lower esophagus
Dilated, elongated, tortuous veins under the esophageal mucosa
Linear ulcers along the lower esophageal mucosa
Fibrous bands crossing the lower esophageal mucosa
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The arrows indicate the dilated, elongated, and tortuous submucosal veins running longitudinally in the lower third of the esophagus.
museum.keyConcept: Esophageal varices: Longitudinal tortuous submucosal venous cords.

museum.text: All of the following are effects of liver cirrhosis EXCEPT:
options: Oesophageal varices at the lower end of the oesophagus
Enlarged, congested spleen with a thick capsule
Dark red spleen with atrophic white pulp
Thickened, fibrosed white portal tracts in the liver
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: All are consequences of liver cirrhosis and chronic venous congestion of the portal system except atrophic white pulp with dark red appearance. In chronic congestive splenomegaly (Banti's disease), the spleen is markedly enlarged and firm with a thick fibrous capsule; cut section shows prominent trabeculae and fibrosis (Gandy-Gamna bodies), not atrophy.
museum.keyConcept: Congestive splenomegaly: Markedly enlarged, firm spleen with thickened capsule and fibrocongestive red pulp expansion.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer of the stomach
Acute gastric erosion of the stomach
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Stomach opened to reveal a solitary, rounded, sharply punched-out ulcer on the lesser curvature of the prepyloric region. The mucosal folds (rugae) radiate symmetrically towards the margins of the ulcer, and the floor is clean and indurated, pathognomonic of a chronic benign peptic ulcer.
museum.keyConcept: Chronic peptic ulcer: Solitary, punched-out mucosal defect with radiating rugae and clean fibrotic base.

museum.text: The orange arrow points to the mucosa around the ulcer. It appears:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In chronic peptic ulcers, the surrounding mucosa is flattened and smooth, with mucosal rugae radiating towards the ulcer crater due to cicatricial contraction of fibrous tissue in the base.
museum.keyConcept: Peptic ulcer gross margin: Smooth, flat margin with radiating rugae.

museum.text: All of the following describe this ulcer EXCEPT:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A hard, wide, infiltrating base is the hallmark of a malignant ulcer (gastric adenocarcinoma). Chronic peptic ulcers feature a sharply punched-out, clean or scarred base limited to the muscularis propria without diffuse infiltration.
museum.keyConcept: Malignant vs benign gastric ulcer: Hard infiltrating base characterizes carcinoma.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer of the pylorus
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Segment of stomach showing marked circumferential mural thickening of the pyloric canal with rigidity and luminal stenosis (napkin-ring / linitis plastica type of infiltrating adenocarcinoma).
museum.keyConcept: Infiltrating pyloric carcinoma: Diffuse circumferential mural thickening causing gastric outlet obstruction.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer of the pylorus
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Segment of stomach showing marked circumferential mural thickening of the pyloric canal with rigidity and luminal stenosis (napkin-ring / linitis plastica type of infiltrating adenocarcinoma).
museum.keyConcept: Infiltrating pyloric carcinoma: Diffuse circumferential mural thickening causing gastric outlet obstruction.

options: Marked circumferential thickening of the pyloric wall by greyish tumour tissue
Marked circumferential thickening of the pyloric wall by whitish fibrous tissue
Marked localized thickening of the pyloric wall by greyish tumour tissue
Marked localized thickening of the gastric body wall by whitish fibrous tissue
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 3 indicates the marked circumferential thickening of the pyloric wall by infiltrative, greyish-white malignant tumor tissue.
museum.keyConcept: Pyloric adenocarcinoma: Circumferential greyish-white mural infiltration.

options: Mucosal infiltration; marked dilatation of the lumen
Muscle infiltration; marked narrowing of the lumen
Muscle infiltration; marked dilatation of the lumen
Serosal infiltration; marked narrowing of the lumen
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 shows diffuse infiltration of the muscularis externa by malignant scirrhous carcinoma, and Label 2 demonstrates severe stenosis (narrowing) of the pyloric lumen.
museum.keyConcept: Linitis plastica / Scirrhous carcinoma: Muscular infiltration producing concentric luminal stenosis.

options: Malignant ulcer of the stomach with gastrojejunostomy
Infiltrating carcinoma of the stomach with gastrojejunostomy
Malignant ulcer of the duodenum with gastroduodenostomy
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Museum jar displaying a segment of stomach with a chronic peptic ulcer anastomosed surgically to an adjacent loop of jejunum (gastrojejunostomy) created to bypass gastric outlet obstruction.
museum.keyConcept: Gastrojejunostomy: Surgical bypass anastomosis between stomach and proximal jejunum for obstructed peptic ulcer.

museum.text: Q13. Labels A, B and C represent respectively:
options: Large ulcer at the pyloric region; opened duodenum and jejunum; normal gastric rugae
Large ulcer at the cardiac region; opened duodenum and jejunum; flattened gastric rugae
Large ulcer at the pyloric region; opened duodenum and ileum; lost gastric rugae
Small ulcer at the pyloric region; opened jejunum and ileum; normal gastric rugae
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gross pathology shows a chronic peptic ulcer at the prepyloric region with surgical gastrojejunostomy.

museum.text: The circled lesion is located at the:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The chronic peptic ulcer is located prepylorically along the lesser curvature.
museum.keyConcept: Gastric ulcer location: Commonly lesser curvature and prepyloric antrum.

museum.text: The  arrow on the right points to:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Mucosal rugae adjacent to the anastomotic stoma are flattened.
museum.keyConcept: Mucosal changes in chronic peptic disease.

options: Raised everted edge; necrotic floor; hard infiltrating base
Flat clear-cut edge; necrotic floor; soft fibrous base
Raised everted edge; clean floor; hard infiltrating base
Flat undermined edge; clean floor; soft fibrous base
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The classic triad of a malignant ulcer (gastric carcinoma): (1) raised everted (rolled-out) margins, (2) necrotic, irregular, hemorrhagic floor, and (3) hard, indurated, deeply infiltrating base.
museum.keyConcept: Triad of malignant ulcer: Raised everted edges, necrotic dirty floor, hard infiltrating base.

museum.text: All of the following are true except  EXCEPT:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A sharply punched-out outline is characteristic of a benign chronic peptic ulcer. Malignant ulcers have irregular, raised, everted margins with diffuse invasion.
museum.keyConcept: Malignant ulcer: Irregular outline with rolled-out edges, not punched-out.

options: Jejunum attached to the duodenum with an artificial opening between their lumina
Jejunum attached to the stomach with an artificial opening between their lumina
Duodenum attached to the stomach with a natural opening between their lumina
Jejunum attached to the stomach with a fistulous tract between their lumina
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gastrojejunostomy consists of an artificial surgical stoma created between the dependent portion of the greater curvature of the stomach and a loop of proximal jejunum.
museum.keyConcept: Gastrojejunostomy: Surgical stoma connecting gastric and jejunal lumina.

museum.text: THis lesion is best characterized as:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Well-defined, solitary crater with dense fibrous base and radiating rugae, diagnostic of a chronic peptic ulcer.

museum.text: All of the following are true about the ulcer  EXCEPT:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Chronic peptic ulcers do NOT have an extensive hard infiltrating base; that finding signifies gastric adenocarcinoma.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer with surrounding fibrosis
Infiltrating carcinoma of the pylorus only
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large, irregular ulcer with prominent raised, rolled, everted margins and a necrotic slough in the floor, diagnostic of ulcerating gastric adenocarcinoma.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer of the stomach
Acute gastric ulcer of the stomach
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large ulcerative lesion with characteristic malignant features: everted boundaries and necrotic base.
Criteria of Identification: Label 1 points to the raised, everted (rolled) tumor margin, while label 2 points to the necrotic, hemorrhagic, dirty floor of the ulcer.

Criteria of Identification: Liver surface is distorted by large, irregular regenerating nodules measuring between 0.5 cm and 3 cm in diameter, separated by broad bands of depressed fibrous tissue, characteristic of macronodular (post-hepatitic) cirrhosis.
museum.keyConcept: Macronodular cirrhosis: Coarse regenerating nodules (>3 mm, up to 2–3 cm) separated by irregular fibrous scars (viral hepatitis B/C etiology).

museum.text: Label 2 points to the nodules. They are:
options: Multiple, round, less than 3 mm in diameter
Multiple, round, 0.5 to 2 cm in diameter
multiple, round, about 5 cm in diameter
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The nodules in macronodular cirrhosis are large, varying from 0.5 to 2 cm in diameter.

options: Low hills and shallow depressions of capsule
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The Glisson's capsule of the cirrhotic liver is chronically thickened and fibrotic.
Criteria of Identification: Prominent large nodules separated by broad fibrous depressions.

museum.text: All of the following are features of this liver EXCEPT:
options: Markedly shrunken with retracted cut section
Normal liver tissue in between the nodules
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In macronodular cirrhosis, the fibrous bands are broad, irregular, and depressed between the regenerating parenchyma.

Criteria of Identification: Cirrhotic liver containing a massive, dominant, yellowish-white, necrotic tumor mass with satellite nodules, representing hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) arising as a complication of cirrhosis.
museum.keyConcept: Hepatocellular carcinoma: Arises on top of HBV/HCV macronodular cirrhosis.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Background of regenerating cirrhotic nodules with a superimposed large neoplastic tumor mass.

museum.text: All of the following describe the spleen in  EXCEPT
options: Dark red with atrophic white pulp
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 points to the main HCC tumor mass, which is bulky, unencapsulated, and shows typical variegated cut surface with areas of yellow necrosis and dark hemorrhage.

options: Laennec’s cirrhosis with nodular cut section
Macronodular cirrhosis with nodular cut section
Bilharzial fibrosis with white portal tracts
Fatty change with yellow bulging surface
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 2 indicates the background cirrhotic regenerative nodules.

museum.text: All of the following are true about the specimens  EXCEPT:
options: The esophagus shows dilated tortuous submucosal veins
The liver shows thickened white portal tracts
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver cut section displaying broad, dense, whitish fibrous collars expanding the portal tracts around portal vein branches resembling the stems of clay pipes ('pipe-stem fibrosis'). Liver lobular architecture is preserved, and true regenerative nodules are absent.
museum.keyConcept: Symmers' pipe-stem fibrosis: Periportal fibrosis around intrahepatic portal branches with preserved parenchymal lobules (non-cirrhotic portal hypertension).

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Dense white fibrous sheaths surrounding portal tracts.

museum.text: All of the following describe the arrowed mass EXCEPT:
options: Greyish with areas of haemorrhage and necrosis
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The white bands are thick sleeves of collagenous scar tissue expanding the portal triads.

options: Cirrhotic nodules in a macronodular cirrhosis
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hepatic parenchyma between the pipe-stem fibrous tracts shows preserved architectural lobulation without pseudolobules.
museum.keyConcept: Preserved lobular architecture in Bilharzial fibrosis.

museum.text: The tissue between the nodules is
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In Schistosoma mansoni pipe-stem fibrosis, the normal lobular architecture of the liver is preserved, distinguishing it from true cirrhosis.

options: Cirrhotic nodules in a macronodular cirrhosis
Cirrhotic nodules in a micronodular cirrhosis
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: All are true EXCEPT impaired liver functions. In Schistosoma pipe-stem fibrosis, hepatocellular synthetic function (albumin, coagulation factors) is preserved until very late, because the hepatocytes themselves are not destroyed.
museum.keyConcept: Preserved hepatocellular function in Bilharzial hepatic fibrosis.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver enlarged and studded with multiple, bilateral, spherical, whitish-tan tumor deposits of varying sizes, many displaying central necrosis and umbilication (central depression), pathognomonic of hematogenous hepatic metastases.
museum.keyConcept: Hepatic metastases: Multiple, variable-sized, bilateral spherical nodules with central umbilication.

options: Multiple, irregular, filled with necrotic liver tissue
Multiple, regular, with thick fibrous walls
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Multiple cannonball nodules scattered throughout both liver lobes.
Criteria of Identification: The central depression in metastatic nodules results from rapid tumor outgrowth of its blood supply, causing ischemic central necrosis and retraction.

museum.text: The cavity wall is lined by:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Key diagnostic hallmark: multiplicity, size variation, and central umbilication.
museum.keyConcept: Gross criteria of secondary liver tumors.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gallbladder opened to reveal a markedly thickened, fibrotic, greyish-white wall and an inflamed mucosal surface containing multiple faceted, yellow-brown gallstones (cholelithiasis).
museum.keyConcept: Chronic calculous cholecystitis: Thick fibrotic wall with multiple faceted gallstones.

options: Thick fibrous wall with chalky white calcification
Thick fibrous wall with irregular necrotic lining
Thin fibrous wall with chalky white calcification
Thin fibrous wall with smooth regular lining
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Classic museum specimen of chronic gallstone disease.

museum.text: The border of this liver is described as:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The wall of the gallbladder is abnormally thickened (often >4-5 mm) by dense fibrous scar tissue.

options: Portal tracts that are thickened, fibrosed and white
Portal tracts that are thickened, fibrosed and yellow
Dilated bile ducts with surrounding fibrosis
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The stones are multiple with flat, polished facet surfaces resulting from mutual friction and compression within the contracted gallbladder.
museum.keyConcept: Faceted gallstones: Mixed stones formed by chronic cholelithiasis and friction.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A thin, translucent wall is normal. Chronic cholecystitis causes dense, thick, opaque, fibrotic mural hypertrophy.

museum.text: The liver tissue between the portal tracts is greyish brown because of:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gallbladder with a thick, contracted wall harboring a solitary, large, rounded, barrel-shaped cholesterol gallstone.
museum.keyConcept: Solitary pure cholesterol gallstone in chronic cholecystitis.

museum.text: All of the following describe these nodules EXCEPT:
options: Separated by fibrous bands with no normal live
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The single stone is large, yellowish, oval, with a smooth surface.
Criteria of Identification: Gallbladder wall is thickened and shrunken around the stone.

Criteria of Identification: Segment of large intestine whose mucosal lining is carpeted by hundreds of small, rounded, sessile and pedunculated adenomatous polyps (>100 polyps), pathognomonic of autosomal dominant FAP (APC gene mutation).
museum.keyConcept: Familial Adenomatous Polyposis: Innumerable adenomatous polyps (>100) carpet the colonic mucosa; 100% progress to adenocarcinoma if untreated.

museum.text: All of the following describe this gall bladder EXCEPT:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hundreds of adenomatous polyps covering the colonic mucosa.

museum.text: The lumen of this opened gall bladder is filled with
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The mucosal surface displays diffuse carpet-like polyposis.

options: Cholesterol stone with hydrops of the gall bladder
Hydrops of the gall bladder without stones
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Untreated FAP carries a 100% lifetime risk of developing invasive colorectal adenocarcinoma by age 40.

museum.text: the arrow points to a complication of this lesion:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Colonic specimen displaying a single discrete pedunculated polyp projecting into the lumen.
Criteria of Identification: The pedunculated polyp consists of a lobulated adenomatous head attached to the mucosa by a narrow fibrovascular stalk.

museum.text: Label 1 points to a structure that is:
options: Blind-ended, about 10 cm long, on the mesenteric border
Blind-ended, about 10 cm long, on the anti-mesenteric border
Open-ended, about 2 cm long, on the anti-mesenteric border
Blind-ended, about 2 cm long, on the mesenteric border
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Adenomatous polyps are true neoplastic lesions (dysplastic), NOT non-neoplastic hamartomas.

options: Tuberculous ulcers of the small intestine
Typhoid ulcers of the small intestine
Amoebic ulcers of the large intestine
Bacillary dysentery of the large intestine
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Segment of sigmoid colon / left colon showing a circumferential, constricting, infiltrating tumor mass encircling the bowel wall like a napkin-ring, causing marked luminal stenosis and proximal dilatation.
museum.keyConcept: Annular carcinoma of left colon: Napkin-ring constricting lesion producing bowel obstruction.

options: Oval, longitudinal, parallel to the direction of the gut
Oval, transverse, perpendicular to the direction of the gut
Oval, transverse, parallel to the direction of the gut
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The tumor grows circumferentially within the bowel wall, constricting the lumen.

museum.text: the yellow arrow points to the ulcer margins. They are:

museum.keyConcept: Proximal bowel dilatation in obstructive colonic carcinoma.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Segment of cecum / ascending colon opened to show a large, bulky, cauliflower-like, friable, exophytic mass projecting into the lumen, typical of right-sided fungating colorectal adenocarcinoma.
museum.keyConcept: Fungating carcinoma of right colon: Exophytic polypoid mass projecting into the spacious cecal lumen.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The mass is exophytic, irregular, and cauliflower-like.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fungating carcinomas occur predominantly in the right colon where the large lumen and liquid feces allow tumors to grow large without early obstruction.
museum.keyConcept: Colorectal cancer location: Fungating in right colon, annular in left colon.

museum.text: The red arrows point to LN that are:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Early obstruction is typical of left-sided annular lesions, NOT right-sided fungating lesions, which present with occult bleeding, anemia, and weakness.
museum.keyConcept: Clinical presentation of right vs left colon cancer.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Colonic mucosa interrupted by a large, deep, irregular ulcer with raised, everted margins and a dirty necrotic base, typical of ulcerating adenocarcinoma.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The floor is necrotic, shaggy, and stained with fecal and blood debris.

Criteria of Identification: Loop of small intestine that is markedly swollen, edematous, congested, and discolored dark blackish-purple with lost luster, resulting from acute mesenteric vascular occlusion (strangulated bowel / mesenteric infarction).
museum.keyConcept: Moist gangrene of bowel: Mesenteric vascular occlusion causing blackish-purple hemorrhagic necrosis and peritonitis.

options: Invagination of one ileal loop into another
Invagination of the terminal ileum into the cecum
Herniation of an ileal loop through the abdominal wall
Twisting of an ileal loop around its mesentery

museum.text: the orange arrow points to the entering loop, which is:

Swollen, bluish, with areas of haemorrhage
Swollen, greyish, with tiny yellow tubercles
Contracted, bluish, with dirty greyish membrane
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Moist gangrene of the intestine is precipitated by sudden arterial thrombosis, mesenteric embolism, or strangulated hernia.
Criteria of Identification: In moist gangrene, the bowel wall is massively thickened, edematous, and covered by dull, foul-smelling fibrinous exudate, NOT thin, dry, or glistening.

museum.text: A 45-year-old man with old pulmonary tuberculosis developed abdominal pain, weight loss, fever and diarrhoea. CT showed ascites, mesenteric lymphadenopathy, thickened peritoneum and multiple nodules. This is the gross appearance of his omentum. What is the diagnosis?

lab.text: What is the nature of this lesion?

Portal fibrosis with preserved liver architecture, chronic specific inflammation
Biliary obstruction with endogenous pigment deposition
Malignant epithelial tumor of viral oncogenesis
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Microscopic slide of the liver shows broad bands of fibrous tissue expanding the portal tracts (pipe-stem fibrosis) while the central veins and parenchymal lobular architecture are preserved, characteristic of hepatic schistosomiasis (Bilharzial liver).
lab.keyConcept: Bilharzial hepatic fibrosis: Portal expansion by fibrous tissue with preserved lobular architecture.

lab.text: the circled structure labeled 1 represents

lab.text: Label 3  represents:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 3 indicates dark brown to blackish Bilharzial pigment (hemozoin-like pigment) engulfed inside the cytoplasm of portal macrophages (histiocytes).
lab.keyConcept: Bilharzial pigment: Dark brown iron-free pigment in portal tract macrophages.

lab.keyConcept: Bilharzial granuloma: Granulomatous response around Schistosoma ova in portal areas.

lab.text: All of the following are true about the lesion in  EXCEPT:

Ova reach the portal tracts as emboli through the portal circulation
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: All are true EXCEPT marked impairment of liver functions. In Bilharzial pipe-stem fibrosis, liver architecture and hepatocellular metabolic/synthetic functions remain remarkably preserved until terminal complications intervene.
lab.keyConcept: Preserved hepatic synthetic function in Bilharzial fibrosis.

lab.text: What is the nature of this lesion?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a primary malignant epithelial neoplasm derived from hepatocytes.
lab.keyConcept: Hepatocellular carcinoma: Malignant epithelial neoplasm.

lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The tumor cells grow in thick, irregular trabeculae (plates >3 cells thick) separated by sinusoidal blood spaces lined by endothelial cells, the classic trabecular (sinusoidal) pattern of HCC.
lab.keyConcept: HCC trabecular pattern: Tumor cell cords >3 cells thick separated by sinusoid-like vascular spaces.

lab.text: The architectural pattern shown is :
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The tumor cells grow in thick, irregular trabeculae (plates >3 cells thick) separated by sinusoidal blood spaces lined by endothelial cells, the classic trabecular (sinusoidal) pattern of HCC.

lab.text: All of the following are features of this legion except
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Malignant cells exhibit an INCREASED nuclear-to-cytoplasmic (N/C) ratio, prominent pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and atypical mitoses; they do not have a decreased N/C ratio.
lab.keyConcept: Cytological criteria of malignancy: Increased N/C ratio.

lab.text: which of the following is true
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Classic trabecular growth pattern.
lab.keyConcept: HCC architecture.

lab.text: label 1 and label 2 represent respectively:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 shows background cirrhotic liver parenchyma with fibrous septa, while label 2 shows the malignant HCC trabeculae.
lab.keyConcept: HCC arising on cirrhosis.

lab.text: all of the following are true about the lesion in EXCEPT:
options: A common predisposing factor in Egypt is HBV and HCV
It is usually preceded by a phase of cirrhosis
It is a malignant epithelial tumor
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: All are true EXCEPT decreased AFP. Serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is significantly ELEVATED in >70% of hepatocellular carcinoma patients and serves as a primary tumor marker.
lab.keyConcept: Tumor markers: Serum AFP is markedly elevated in HCC.

lab.text: what stain is used, and what do the bluish areas (arrows) represent?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Masson's trichrome stain selectively colors collagenous fibrous connective tissue bright blue, clearly delineating the bridging fibrous septa that encircle regenerating hepatocytes in cirrhosis.
lab.keyConcept: Special stains: Masson's trichrome stains collagen / fibrous septa blue.

lab.text: The areas outlined by the red dotted lines in are:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Outlined areas represent rounded regenerative parenchymal nodules lacking central veins and surrounded completely by fibrous scars.
lab.keyConcept: Regenerative nodules in cirrhosis.

lab.text: What is the nature of the lesion
options: Diffuse hepatic fibrosis with regenerative liver nodules
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Triad of cirrhosis: diffuse parenchymal bridging fibrosis, loss of normal lobular architecture, and parenchymal nodular regeneration.
lab.keyConcept: Histological definition of cirrhosis: Diffuse fibrosis + regenerative nodules + architectural distortion.

lab.text: All of the following are found here EXCEPT:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In chronic cirrhosis, the inflammatory infiltrate consists of lymphocytes, plasma cells, and histiocytes; acute neutrophils are not a typical feature unless acute alcoholic hepatitis or sepsis is superimposed.
lab.keyConcept: Chronic inflammatory infiltrate in cirrhosis.

lab.text: All of the following are true about the lesion   EXCEPT:
options: The commonest cause in Egypt is viral hepatitis
It presents with portal hypertension manifestations
It is a predisposing factor for HCC
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Unlike pure Bilharzial fibrosis, true liver cirrhosis causes progressive hepatocellular functional failure (hypoalbuminemia, coagulopathy, jaundice).
lab.keyConcept: Impaired liver function in cirrhosis.

lab.text: Which of the following best describes the structures indicated by the yellow arrows?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hepatocytes distended by large single intracytoplasmic lipid droplets that displace the nucleus to the cell periphery (signet-ring appearance), diagnostic of macrovesicular steatosis (fatty liver).
lab.keyConcept: Macrovesicular steatosis: Single large fat vacuole displacing the hepatocyte nucleus.

lab.text: What is the nature of the lesion
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Steatosis represents abnormal accumulation of triglycerides within parenchymal liver cells.
lab.keyConcept: Pathogenesis of hepatic steatosis.

lab.text: What is the nature of the lesion
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Intrahepatic bile stasis manifests as yellow-green to brown bile plugs within dilated canaliculi and hepatocytes, representing endogenous pigment deposition.
lab.keyConcept: Cholestasis: Endogenous bile pigment accumulation.

lab.text: labels 1, 2 and 3 represent respectively:
options: Proliferated bile ductules; bile accumulations; fibrosis and chronic inflammatory infiltrate
Angiomatoids; bile accumulations; fibrosis and chronic inflammatory infiltrate
Proliferated bile ductules; bile accumulations; lymphoid stroma
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Classic histopathological triad of biliary obstruction in the portal tract.
lab.keyConcept: Histology of extrahepatic biliary obstruction.

lab.text: All of the following are true about the lesion EXCEPT:
options: The patient presents with yellow skin and sclera
It may progress to liver cirrhosis
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Full-thickness gastric mucosal defect showing the 4 classical zones of Askanazy: (1) superficial necrotic exudate, (2) fibrinoid necrosis, (3) vascular granulation tissue, and (4) deep fibrous collagenous scar.
lab.keyConcept: Four histological zones of chronic peptic ulcer.

lab.text: What is the nature of the lesion
options: Benign encapsulated mixed salivary gland tumor
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The deepest zone of a chronic peptic ulcer is dense, hypocellular collagenous scar tissue replacing the muscularis propria.
lab.keyConcept: Deepest zone of peptic ulcer: Fibrous scar.

lab.text: the red star marks:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Acute appendicitis is defined histopathologically by acute suppurative inflammation characterized by heavy neutrophilic infiltration extending transmurally through the muscularis propria.
lab.keyConcept: Diagnostic hallmark of acute appendicitis: Neutrophilic infiltration of muscularis propria.

lab.text: The cells lining this legion are
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Transmural neutrophilic infiltration through the muscularis propria is the definitive diagnostic criterion.
lab.keyConcept: Microscopic diagnosis of acute appendicitis.

lab.text: All of the following are true about the lesion  EXCEPT:
options: It is also called papillary cystadenoma lymphomatosum
It contains chondroid and myxoid stroma
Cystic spaces may show intraluminal papillary projections
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Well-circumscribed salivary gland tumor exhibiting both epithelial structures (ducts, tubules, sheets) and mesenchymal-like myxoid, chondroid, and hyaline stroma, diagnostic of pleomorphic adenoma (mixed tumor).
lab.keyConcept: Pleomorphic adenoma: Biphasic mixed tumor composed of epithelial ducts and myxochondroid stroma.

lab.text: What is the nature of the lesion
options: Benign encapsulated mixed salivary gland tumor
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Characteristically benign, encapsulated, and composed of mixed morphological components.
lab.keyConcept: Nature of pleomorphic adenoma.

lab.text: labels A and B represent respectively:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The 'pleomorphic' designation refers to the mixture of ductal/myoepithelial cells with chondromyxoid matrix.
lab.keyConcept: Biphasic architecture.

lab.text: All of the following are true about the lesion EXCEPT:
options: It has epithelial duct-like structures with spindle myoepithelial cells
Its mesenchymal elements include myxoid tissue with chondroid islands
It is most common in the parotid gland
Its stroma is rich in lymphoid follicles with germinal centers
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Colonic polyp characterized by cystically dilated mucin-filled glands lined by bland, non-dysplastic columnar and goblet cells, embedded in abundant, vascular, inflamed stroma.
lab.keyConcept: Juvenile polyp: Hamartomatous polyp with cystically dilated retention glands and no dysplasia.

lab.text: The dashed arrows indicate inflammatory involvement of which structure?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Prominent large, cyst-like glands filled with pink mucin.
lab.keyConcept: Cystic glandular dilatation in retention polyps.

lab.text: What is the nature of this lesion?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The epithelium lining the cystic spaces is mature, bland, and non-dysplastic.
lab.keyConcept: Bland non-dysplastic epithelium.

lab.text: Which of the following best identifies the circled structure?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: All are true EXCEPT neoplastic/dysplastic nature. Juvenile polyps are NON-neoplastic hamartomas with zero intrinsic dysplasia.
lab.keyConcept: Juvenile polyps are non-neoplastic hamartomas.

lab.text: All of the following are histopathological findings of this legion EXCEPT:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Acute appendicitis does not feature malignant glands; it is characterized by acute inflammation, mucosal ulceration, neutrophils, and vascular congestion.
lab.keyConcept: Acute appendiceal histology.

lab.text: What is the most likely diagnosis?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Classic retention polyp with cystically dilated crypts and inflamed stroma.
lab.keyConcept: Juvenile polyp.

lab.text: Which of the following is the characteristic microscopic finding?
options: Crowded malignant glands invading the muscularis propria
Hyperchromatic dysplastic epithelium with nuclear pseudostratification
Pools of extracellular mucin containing malignant cells
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Colonic polyp showing crowded, elongated, branching glands lined by dysplastic epithelium with nuclear pseudostratification, hyperchromasia, and loss of goblet cells (tubular adenoma).
lab.keyConcept: Adenomatous polyp: Benign neoplastic polyp with epithelial dysplasia (pre-cancerous).

lab.text: Which of the following best describes the epithelial lining of the dilated glands?
options: Malignant columnar cells with marked atypia
Bland columnar cells with goblet cells
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Microscopic feature correctly identified as Malignant columnar cells with marked atypia.
lab.keyConcept: Pathology lab spotter: Malignant columnar cells with marked atypia.

lab.text: What is the most likely diagnosis?

lab.keyConcept: Juvenile polyp.

lab.text: Which of the following is the hallmark feature of this lesion?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Colonic polyp showing crowded, elongated, branching glands lined by dysplastic epithelium with nuclear pseudostratification, hyperchromasia, and loss of goblet cells (tubular adenoma).
lab.keyConcept: Adenomatous polyp: Benign neoplastic polyp with epithelial dysplasia (pre-cancerous).

lab.text: All of the following are true about this legion EXCEPT:
options: Their characteristic glands are lined by bland, non-dysplastic epithelium with goblet cells.
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Epithelial dysplasia (nuclear stratification, hyperchromasia, mitoses) is the definitive diagnostic hallmark distinguishing adenomas from non-neoplastic polyps.
lab.keyConcept: Hallmark of adenoma: Epithelial dysplasia.

lab.text: Which of the following best describes the nature of this lesion?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: All are true EXCEPT bland non-dysplastic lining. Adenomas are ALWAYS characterized by dysplastic epithelium.
lab.keyConcept: Adenoma dysplasia requirement.

lab.text: Which of the following statements about this legion  is CORRECT?
options: They are always malignant at the time of diagnosis.
High-grade dysplasia may progress to carcinoma in situ and then adenocarcinoma.
They are characterized by cystically dilated glands without dysplasia.
They are always associated with a fibrovascular core.
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tubular adenomas are benign neoplasms that serve as premalignant precursor lesions for colorectal adenocarcinoma.
lab.keyConcept: Premalignant potential of adenomas.

lab.text: Which of the following features is most characteristic of the epithelial changes indicated by the arrows?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Adenoma-carcinoma sequence: progressive accumulation of mutations causes transition from low-grade to high-grade dysplasia, intramucosal carcinoma, and invasive adenocarcinoma.
lab.keyConcept: Adenoma-carcinoma sequence.

lab.text: identify the structure indicated by the right arrow.
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Arrows demonstrate elongated, dark, hyperchromatic nuclei stacked upon one another (pseudostratification), typical of low-grade dysplasia.
lab.keyConcept: Cytological features of low-grade dysplasia.

lab.text: A histopathological examination of a colonic tumor reveals malignant glands of variable size and shape. The glands are lined by one or more layers of malignant cells and invade through the basement membrane into the submucosa.
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Arrow points to the adjacent normal colonic mucosa with straight crypts and abundant goblet cells.
lab.keyConcept: Normal colonic crypt architecture.

lab.text: What is the most likely diagnosis?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Irregular, crowded, infiltrative malignant glands invading through the muscularis mucosae into the submucosa, lined by pleomorphic, hyperchromatic malignant cells, diagnostic of invasive adenocarcinoma.
lab.keyConcept: Colorectal adenocarcinoma: Malignant glands infiltrating through muscularis mucosae.

lab.text: All of the following are true about this legion EXCEPT:
options: It may present with bleeding per rectum.
It may present with irregular bowel habits.
It may appear as an ulcerating, fungating or infiltrating mass.
Its malignant glands may invade the submucosa.
Its epithelial cells show no nuclear atypia.
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Irregular, crowded, infiltrative malignant glands invading through the muscularis mucosae into the submucosa, lined by pleomorphic, hyperchromatic malignant cells, diagnostic of invasive adenocarcinoma.
lab.keyConcept: Colorectal adenocarcinoma: Malignant glands infiltrating through muscularis mucosae.

lab.text: All of the following are characteristic microscopic features of this legion EXCEPT:
options: Glands variable in size and shape
Cystically dilated glands lined by bland columnar
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: All are true EXCEPT absence of nuclear atypia. Colorectal adenocarcinoma cells ALWAYS display marked cytological atypia, pleomorphism, and atypical mitoses.
lab.keyConcept: Malignant cytological atypia.
